text: When he came back to Capernaum a few days later, word spread that he was at home.
So many people gathered that there was no room left, not even outside the door, and he was speaking the word to them.
Then some men came, bringing to him a paralyzed man carried by four of them.

versions.text: Then some men came, bringing him a paralyzed man carried by four of them.
versions.explanation: "bringing him a paralyzed man" reads as though the man were a gift being handed over; "bringing to him" is clearer for oral reading and matches the Greek πρὸς αὐτόν.

text: Since they could not bring the man to Jesus because of the crowd, they opened up the roof above him, dug through it, and lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man was lying.

versions.text: Since they could not get to him because of the crowd, they opened up the roof above him, dug through it, and lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man was lying.
versions.explanation: The Greek προσενέγκαι αὐτῷ means "to bring [the paralyzed man] to him," not merely that the carriers could not reach Jesus themselves. The current wording loses the object of the action.

text: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, "Son, your sins are forgiven."
Some of the scribes were sitting there, reasoning in their hearts,

versions.text: Some of the scribes were sitting there, and they were thinking to themselves,
versions.explanation: The Greek specifies "in their hearts," which also sets up Jesus' reply in verse 8 ("in your hearts"). Keeping the wording preserves the deliberate echo.

text: "Why does this man talk like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
At once Jesus knew in his spirit that this was what they were thinking, and he said to them, "Why are you turning these things over in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up, take your mat and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—he said to the paralyzed man,
"I say to you: get up, take your mat, and go home."
The man got up, and immediately took his mat and walked out in front of them all. Everyone was astounded and praised God, saying, "We have never seen anything like this!"
Jesus went out again beside the sea. The whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
As he walked along, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, "Follow me." And he got up and followed him.
Later, as Jesus was reclining at table in Levi's house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with him and his disciples—for there were many who followed him.
When the scribes of the Pharisees saw that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, they said to his disciples, "Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
Hearing this, Jesus said to them, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
Now John's disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. Some people came and asked him, "Why do John's disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not?"
Jesus answered, "Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and on that day they will fast.
No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. If he does, the patch pulls away from it—new from old—and the tear becomes worse.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the skins are ruined. No, new wine goes into fresh wineskins."
One Sabbath he was passing through the grainfields, and his disciples began to make their way along, picking heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, "Look, why are they doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?"
He said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him?
He entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which only the priests are permitted to eat, and he gave some to those who were with him."
Then he said to them, "The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
